standard_prerequisites.name: Splitting fields and similar algebras of prescribed degree
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the existence, for a finite splitting field, of an algebra in the same Brauer class whose degree is the square of the degree of the splitting field.

standard_prerequisites.name: Similarity and matrix algebras over a skew field
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the algebra obtained is a matrix algebra over the given skew field, which gives its degree in terms of the size of the matrix and the degree of the skew field.

core_obligations: The algebra of prescribed degree (proof lines 913-916): the cited theorem produces a finite central simple algebra in the Brauer class of the skew field whose degree is the square of the degree of the splitting field.

The divisibility (proof lines 917-919): by similarity that algebra is a matrix algebra over the skew field, so its degree is the product of the size of the matrix and the degree of the skew field; comparing with the previous equality and taking square roots gives the divisibility of the degree of the splitting field by the degree of the skew field.
proof_roadmap: Produce a similar algebra whose degree is the square of the splitting field degree.
Write it as a matrix algebra over the skew field to compute its degree.
Compare the two expressions and take square roots.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a finite central skew field of degree d, every finite splitting field has degree over the ground field divisible by d (statement lines 906-911). The proof is a complete argument: the characterization of splitting fields produces an algebra in the same Brauer class whose degree is the square of the degree of the splitting field (proof lines 913-916), and by similarity that algebra is a matrix algebra over the skew field, so its degree is the size of the matrix times the degree of the skew field; comparing and taking square roots gives the divisibility (proof lines 917-919). The non-formal content is the comparison of the two degree computations. The claim is H2.
